headline: Stalingrad surrendered in February, the Warsaw Ghetto fought for a month, and Italy changed sides
texture: The German Sixth Army surrendered at Stalingrad on February 2. The Warsaw Ghetto Uprising began on April 19 when German troops entered to clear it, and ended on May 16 with thirteen thousand Jews killed inside the ghetto. The Afrika Korps and the Italian forces in North Africa surrendered on May 13. Italy signed an armistice at Cassibile in September and Eisenhower announced it publicly.

Roosevelt and Churchill met at Casablanca between January 14 and 24, and in November the two of them met Stalin at Tehran. An agreement founding the United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration was signed on November 9, which put a name to what would come after.

This Is the Army took $8,301,000 in rentals, more than double the year's fifth-place film, with the profits going to army relief. Casablanca won Best Picture. The Mills Brothers had the year's best-selling record with Paper Doll. Nikola Tesla died in January and Sergei Rachmaninoff in the spring, both in American exile.
